title: Interactive Apps
text: Seven Shiny applications covering data analysis, visualization and modelling. Each one ships inside its own R package and runs locally — there is no hosted copy to sign up for, and nothing to install beyond the package itself.

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Regression and modelling




olsrr

Linear regression

Interactive regression output, diagnostics and variable selection.


Interactive diagnostics for a fitted lm model.

install.packages("olsrr")
olsrr::ols_launch_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub







blorr

Logistic regression

Model fit, validation and collinearity for binary outcomes.


The glm equivalent of the olsrr app.

install.packages("blorr")
blorr::blr_launch_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub







rfm

Customer segmentation

Generate RFM scores and explore customer segments visually.


Point it at transaction- or customer-level data.

install.packages("rfm")
rfm::rfm_launch_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Statistics and distributions




descriptr

Descriptive statistics

Data screening, summary statistics, frequency and cross tables.


A visual front end to the descriptr functions.

install.packages("descriptr")
descriptr::ds_launch_shiny_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub







inferr

Hypothesis testing

t tests, chi square, binomial and proportion tests, interactively.


Choose the test, pick the columns, read the result.

install.packages("inferr")
inferr::ifr_launch_shiny_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub



Also exported


inferr exports a second launcher under a longer name, infer_launch_shiny_app(). It is the same app; ifr_launch_shiny_app() is used here for consistency with the other packages.








vistributions

Probability distributions

Visualize the binomial, chi square, normal, F and t distributions.


Adjust the parameters and watch the density update.

install.packages("vistributions")
vistributions::vdist_launch_app()

Docs CRAN GitHub

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Everything in one app
xplorerr bundles the whole set behind a single install, and adds a visualizer the other packages do not have. If you are not attached to a particular package, start here.



xplorerr

All seven apps

Descriptive, inferential, visual, RFM, linear and logistic — one package, one install.


Seven launchers. Each opens its own app window.

install.packages("xplorerr")
xplorerr::app_linear_regression()   # linear regression
xplorerr::app_logistic_regression() # logistic regression
xplorerr::app_descriptive()         # descriptive statistics
xplorerr::app_inference()           # hypothesis testing
xplorerr::app_vistributions()       # probability distributions
xplorerr::app_rfm_analysis()        # RFM / customer segmentation
xplorerr::app_visualizer()          # data visualization

Docs CRAN GitHub

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Which launcher should I use?
Both routes work and reach the same apps. The difference is who owns them.



Option A

One install, seven apps

Install xplorerr and call any app_*() function. Nothing else to install.


Best if you want the visualizer, or several apps at once.






Option B

The owning package

Install the package that owns the app and call its own launcher.


Best if you already use that package for its non-interactive functions.


Package reference











nse2r has no app here



nse2r did ship a Shiny app for NSE market data, but the package was archived on CRAN on 2023-08-07 and is under revival, so it gets no app card. Nothing to install and nothing to link to.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
I build statistical software that holds up outside a tutorial, and I help teams do the same. My work sits where R, statistics, economics and finance overlap — regression diagnostics, customer segmentation, descriptive and inferential statistics, and the unglamorous plumbing that keeps an analysis reproducible six months later when someone else has to rerun it.
Most of that work is open source. The package portfolio below is used far more widely than I expected when I started writing it, and it is the reason people find their way here: the packages are free, the vignettes are free, and there is no upsell attached to any of it.
I also write. Six data science textbooks are free to read online, and I founded Rsquared Academy, an open-source education platform for data science, where the courses behind those books live.
I earned my postgraduate degree from Madras School of Economics (Anna University), Chennai, and now maintain the portfolio independently from Bengaluru, India.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Teaching
I run Rsquared Academy, where the courses behind the books are taught in full. It is an open-source education platform, not a lead-generation funnel — the course material is written to be useful even if you never sign up for anything.

For individuals. Self-paced and live courses on R, the tidyverse, visualization, SQL and command-line tooling.
For teams. Masterclasses built around your own data and problems, run as hands-on sessions rather than lectures.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Consulting & Advisory
Custom package development and architecture. Internal R or Python tooling built to survive handover: documented, tested, and structured so your team can extend it without me. Most consulting work is undocumented code that one person understands, and that is a single point of failure I can help remove.
Team masterclasses. Tidyverse, SQL, command-line tooling. Built around your data, your conventions and your team’s existing stack.
Who this is for: teams shipping quantitative work that other people have to maintain. Who it is not for: one-off analyses, or anyone looking for a pre-packaged answer.

title: E-Books
text:
Learning path
The Core Track is designed to be followed end to end. The two companions slot in alongside it rather than after it.


Core 01

Intro to R

BeginnerZero to running code. RStudio, packages, help.




Core 02

Data Wrangling

BeginnerImport, reshape, dplyr, pipes, tibbles.




Core 03

Viz with ggplot2

IntermediateGrammar of graphics through to publication polish.




Core 04

R, Databases & SQL

IntermediateDBI, dbplyr, queries, joins.

Shortcut: already wrangling data in SQL? Take 04 straight after 02.





Companion A — Foundational Tooling

Command Line Basics

BeginnerFiles, permissions, pipes and scripting for R users. Pair with Core 01.


On Windows: everything works from the RStudio Terminal, Git Bash or WSL — chapter 1 covers all three.




Companion B — Graphics Deep-Dive

Data Viz with Base R

IntermediateBase graphics engine, parameters, multi-panel layouts, production export. Zero dependencies. After Core 03.
